title: Piano Sonata No. 21 in B-flat major
hook: Schubert’s last sonata, finished eight weeks before he died, with a low trill that haunts its calm.

painting.title: View of Dresden by Moonlight
painting.pairingNote: A quiet river city under the moon, painted by a contemporary of Schubert; the sonata’s calm, nocturnal glow and its long silences.

facts: Schubert wrote his last three piano sonatas in September 1828 and finished this one on the 26th. Two days later he played from them at an evening gathering in Vienna. He died on 19 November, aged 31.

No publisher took them in his lifetime. Anton Diabelli published them about ten years later and dedicated them to Robert Schumann, because Johann Nepomuk Hummel, the pianist Schubert had chosen, had died.

The first movement is long and unhurried, marked *Molto moderato*. Its calm opening melody is broken by a soft, low [[trill|trill]] deep in the bass, a sound that comes back at the movement’s key moments.
Schubert writes for the piano as for a singer: long melodies in the middle of the keyboard, with the [[sustain-pedal|sustain pedal]] letting the harmonies ring around them.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a calm song haunted by a trill (I), a lament over a rocking rhythm (II), a light, delicate scherzo (III), a finale that seems to start in the wrong key and finds its way home (IV).

movements.heading: Molto moderato
movements.summary: A long movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] built on a quiet, hymn-like melody. Its [[exposition|exposition]] moves through three keys instead of the usual two, and a low trill keeps opening doors into distant ones.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a calm, singing melody in the middle of the keyboard over soft, even chords.

mainIdeas.name: The trill
mainIdeas.description: a soft rumble on a low G-flat, far below the melody, followed by silence.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a darker melody in F-sharp minor over a pulsing accompaniment in threes.

stops.hear: A calm, hymn-like melody in the middle of the keyboard over soft chords
Deep in the bass, a soft, rumbling trill; then silence

stops.hear: The melody slips into a distant, veiled key
stops.happening: A turn to G-flat major, the key the trill hinted at

stops.hear: Darker, in a new key; a melody over a pulsing accompaniment in threes
Brighter, in F major; quicker, dancing figures
stops.happening: The third key of the exposition

stops.hear: Suddenly loud: the low trill erupts, and a few bars appear that are heard nowhere else

stops.hear: The calm opening melody again
A new, wandering melody in a minor key
Soft, repeated chords
stops.happening: A near-quotation of the piano part of Schubert’s own [[lied|lied]] “Der Wanderer”

stops.hear: A loud climax; then the opening melody, quietly, in D minor
stops.happening: The turning point of the development

The opening melody, back in B-flat major

notice: Count the silences. After almost every trill Schubert writes a pause, and the music waits before it goes on.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Uchida plays the exposition repeat, including the first-time bars at ≈ 5:20, which exist only if the repeat is taken. Pianists disagree: András Schiff has called leaving them out “the amputation of a limb”, while Alfred Brendel (also recommended here) omits the repeat.

movements.heading: Andante sostenuto
movements.summary: A slow movement in C-sharp minor, a key very far from the sonata’s home. A grave melody moves over a rocking rhythm; a hymn-like middle section brings warmth, and one sudden change of key near the end is like a door opening.

mainIdeas.name: The main melody
mainIdeas.description: slow and grave, in the middle of the keyboard, over a rocking figure in which the left hand reaches over the right to touch high notes.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: a hymn-like melody in A major over a flowing, rippling accompaniment.

stops.hear: A slow, grave melody; around it, a rocking figure that reaches from the bass up above the tune
stops.happening: The main section, in C-sharp minor. The pedal blurs the notes into one sound

stops.hear: Warmer: a hymn-like melody in the middle, over a flowing, rippling accompaniment
stops.happening: The middle section, in A major

stops.hear: The grave melody returns; the rocking figure is slightly changed
A sudden, soft shift into a bright, distant key
stops.happening: C major, then E major: the surprise of the movement

stops.hear: The major key at last, still shadowed by the minor; a very quiet close

notice: Wait for the key change at ≈ 8:20. Nothing gets louder; only the harmony turns, and the light changes.

movements.heading: Scherzo. Allegro vivace con delicatezza
movements.summary: A short, quick [[scherzo|scherzo]], marked “with delicacy”. It is light and playful, with a darker [[trio|trio]] in the minor.

stops.hear: Quick, light, detached figures, soft and playful
A bouncy new tune in a distant key
stops.happening: The middle of the scherzo, in D-flat major

stops.hear: Darker and heavier, with stubborn accents off the beat
The light figures again

movements.heading: Allegro ma non troppo – Presto
movements.summary: A [[rondo|rondo]]-like finale. Its theme begins on a bare, held octave and seems to start in the wrong key, then finds its way to B-flat. It ends with a fast, loud dash.

mainIdeas.name: The main theme
mainIdeas.description: a single held octave on G, then a skipping tune that sounds like C minor before it settles in B-flat major.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a long, flowing melody over an unbroken stream of quick notes.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 3
mainIdeas.description: a loud, stamping theme in F minor with a dotted rhythm.

stops.hear: One bare octave, G, held; then a skipping tune that takes a while to find its key
A long, flowing melody over a continuous stream of quick notes
A pause, then a loud, stamping theme in a dotted rhythm; it melts into a soft version of itself
stops.happening: Theme 3, in F minor, then F major

stops.hear: The bare octave and the skipping tune
The main tune’s rhythm driven through distant keys to a climax, then a long, quietening descent
The bare octave again
The tune breaks into fragments separated by silences, each landing somewhere unexpected
Fast and loud, a rush to the final chords

notice: Listen to the held G at ≈ 0:00. Alfred Brendel hears it as the answer to the low trill of the first movement.

threads.title: The trill
threads.body: The first movement’s low trill on G-flat leads to every distant key in the sonata; the finale’s bare G seems to answer it.

threads.title: Far-away keys
threads.body: G-flat, F-sharp minor, C-sharp minor: the sonata keeps wandering from B-flat, like the wanderer of the song it quotes.

threads.title: Silence
threads.body: Pauses after the trills, fragments in the finale’s coda: Schubert lets the music stop and listen.
